headword: {三色団子|さんしょくだんご}

definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese sweet consisting of three rice dumplings on a skewer, each a different color: pink (or red), white, and green. Strongly associated with cherry blossom viewing (hanami) and spring.

examples.japanese: {花見|はなみ}には{三色団子|さんしょくだんご}が{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: Three-colored dango are essential for cherry blossom viewing.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちが{三色団子|さんしょくだんご}を{嬉|うれ}しそうに{食|た}べていた。
examples.english: The children were happily eating three-colored dango.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になると、{和菓子屋|わがしや}の{店先|みせさき}に{三色団子|さんしょくだんご}が{並|なら}び、{桜|さくら}の{季節|きせつ}の{訪|おとず}れを{感|かん}じさせてくれる。
examples.english: When spring arrives, three-colored dango line the shelves of Japanese sweet shops, reminding us that cherry blossom season has come.

notes:
Also called {花見団子|はなみだんご}. The three colors traditionally represent the seasons of spring: pink ({桜|さくら}, cherry blossoms), white ({雪|ゆき}, the last snow of winter), and green ({蓬|よもぎ}, fresh mugwort sprouts). Some interpretations link the colors to the progression of cherry blossoms: pink buds, white full bloom, and green leaves after the petals fall.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三色団子|さんしょくだんご}を{食|た}べる: to eat three-colored dango
- {三色団子|さんしょくだんご}を{作|つく}る: to make three-colored dango
- {串|くし}に{刺|さ}した{三色団子|さんしょくだんご}: three-colored dango on a skewer

CULTURAL NOTE:
The saying {花|はな}より{団子|だんご} (dango over flowers) humorously expresses the preference for practical pleasures like eating over aesthetic ones like viewing blossoms. {三色団子|さんしょくだんご} is one of the iconic treats behind this proverb. Available year-round at many shops, but peak season is March through April.
